clue.text: Room near to West End

parts.note: close means near

indicators.note: the end of the word West is its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone describes a room handily placed for London's theatre district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West End' looks like London's theatre district, but 'End' asks for the last letter of 'West', T. 'to' only joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A closet is a small private chamber or cupboard-sized space in a house.

clue.text: There's a great deal to this game

parts.note: a lot is a great deal
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that there is plenty involved in some game.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotto is a game of chance like bingo, where numbers are drawn.

clue.text: Wisely, say, consuming food — not till lunch starts

indicators.note: the word say swallows the other pieces, as if eating them

parts.note: taken as written
a pie is a kind of food

indicators.note: the starts of not, till and lunch are their first letters

explanation.surface: Someone advises, sensibly, against eating before lunchtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts' covers all three words of 'not till lunch', not just the last; 'consuming' means the food and the initials are eaten by 'say'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapient means wise or sagacious, so the adverb means sagely.

clue.text: The Trojan leader is one who bore Achilles

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the leader of the word Trojan is its first letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark about a Trojan commander and the hero Achilles from the Trojan War.
explanation.walkthrough: The Trojan War setting suggests Hector or Aeneas, but 'leader' just takes the first letter of 'Trojan'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the sea-nymph Thetis was the mother of Achilles.

clue.text: Marks given in one article about Leo for instance

indicators.note: the pieces from in, one and article wrap round the zodiac piece

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral I is one
a is the indefinite article
Leo is an example of a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: An astrology column in which marks are awarded in an item on Leo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leo for instance' is a definition by example: Leo is one of the zodiac signs. 'about' wraps the in-one-article string round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Insignia are badges or emblems, distinguishing marks of rank or office.

clue.text: Bad penny coin — surely I can use it to cover myself

indicators.note: bad suggests the letters are spoilt and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who has been handed a dud coin decides it can at least serve as protection.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the P of 'penny' joins the fodder; COIN SURELY I CAN supplies the rest of the fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A policy taken out with an insurer protects you against loss, providing cover.

clue.text: Time may be for word sequence

definitions.meaning: a term of imprisonment, as in doing time
a run of words forming a complete grammatical statement

explanation.surface: Someone suggests that time could stand in for a series of words.
explanation.definitionFit: A prison term is time served, and a grammatical unit is a string of words.

clue.text: Award for Ulysses

definitions.meaning: a sum of money given, such as a student's
the first name of the eighteenth US president

explanation.surface: A prize presented in honour of someone called Ulysses.
explanation.definitionFit: A bursary or sum given is an award, and Ulysses S. Grant was the US general and president.

clue.text: Examples of positions taken by ruling party

indicators.note: the stances follow the ruling party, which takes them up first

parts.note: the party in power is said to be in
stances are positions or postures

explanation.surface: A political comment on the stands adopted by the government.
explanation.definitionFit: Instances are cases or illustrations of something.

clue.text: Engineer's female relative pursues a degree

parts.note: a step is a degree on a scale
a hen is a female bird
a son is a relative

explanation.surface: A female relation of an engineer is studying for a university degree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pursues' looks like studying, but it places the relative piece last. George Stephenson was the British railway engineer behind the Rocket locomotive.
explanation.definitionFit: George and Robert Stephenson were famous British railway engineers; the 's reads as 'is'.

clue.text: Oriental. well back in the recess.

indicators.note: back means the word for a well is read backwards

parts.note: a spa is a spring or well
E stands for East, the Orient

explanation.surface: Someone from the East sits well back in an alcove.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is a semicircular recess at the end of a church.

clue.text: Toil here perhaps for the lodging house keeper

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Someone toils here, at a guesthouse, as its manager.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotelier runs an inn or guesthouse.

clue.text: Sydney's sundries are not in the basic price

definitions.meaning: the Australian cricket name for runs not hit off the bat
add-ons charged in addition to the standard fee

explanation.surface: Australian odds and ends are charged on top of the basic price.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, runs from byes and wides are extras in Britain but sundries in Australia, hence 'Sydney's'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australian cricket the runs not scored off the bat are called sundries, and add-ons cost more.

clue.text: Sandwich once, and a drink

definitions.meaning: the Kent town was formerly a harbour town
a sweet fortified wine from Portugal

explanation.surface: A snack and a beverage are ordered.
explanation.walkthrough: Sandwich is a town in Kent that was once a major harbour, one of the Cinque Ports, before its harbour silted up.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandwich in Kent was one of the Cinque Ports, a harbour town, and port is a fortified wine.

clue.text: Not noticing about £1, it's clear

indicators.note: the word for clear goes around the letters for one pound

parts.note: obvious means clear or evident
L is the pound sign and I is one

explanation.surface: Someone notices nothing about a pound coin, since it is clear.
explanation.walkthrough: '£1' gives L (pound, from Latin libra) and I (one), placed inside OBVIOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Being oblivious means being unaware of what is around you.

clue.text: Impudence to add spirit to adornment

parts.note: neck is cheek or impudence
to lace a drink is to add spirits to it

explanation.surface: It is cheeky to spike a drink with alcohol as an ornament.
explanation.definitionFit: A necklace is jewellery worn round the neck as decoration.

clue.text: Plant, appears reddish brown with scrap

parts.note: liver is a reddish-brown colour
an ort is a scrap of leftover food

explanation.surface: A plant shows a reddish-brown colour along with a small fragment.
explanation.definitionFit: Liverwort is a small flowerless plant related to mosses.

clue.text: In verbal form? Not one penny piece.

indicators.note: not means the letters for one and penny are left out of the grammar word

parts.note: a participle is a form of a verb, like going or gone
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A grammar question, followed by someone insisting they will not pay a single penny.
explanation.definitionFit: A particle is a tiny bit or fragment.

clue.text: One of those Lamb had in childhood

definitions.text: One of those Lamb had in childhood

parts.words: One of those Lamb had in childhood
parts.note: Charles Lamb's poem The Old Familiar Faces says he had companions to play with in his days of childhood

explanation.surface: A recollection of what someone named Lamb had when young.
explanation.walkthrough: Lamb is the essayist Charles Lamb, not a young sheep; his poem The Old Familiar Faces begins 'I have had playmates, I have had companions, In my days of childhood'.
explanation.definitionFit: A playmate is a childhood friend you play with.

clue.text: Famous Day Street garment

parts.note: VE Day, Victory in Europe Day, is a famous date

explanation.surface: A well-known celebrity's clothing shop on a high street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Famous Day' looks like the film star Doris Day; it is VE Day, 8 May 1945. In Britain a vest is an undershirt.
explanation.definitionFit: A vest is a sleeveless undergarment or waistcoat.

clue.text: Note very loud one — to delete

parts.note: E is a musical note
ff, fortissimo, means very loud in music
an ace is a one in cards

explanation.surface: A musical score marking: a note, played very loudly, is to be deleted.
explanation.definitionFit: To efface something is to rub it out or erase it.

clue.text: A check about commander getting the bird

indicators.note: the word for check wraps round the commander's letters

parts.note: to vet is to check
OC is Officer Commanding

explanation.surface: An inspection of a commanding officer ends with him being booed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting the bird' suggests being jeered; here it just links to the bird, a wading bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocet is a wading bird with an upcurved bill.

clue.text: About four found wandering 'in the island

parts.note: c stands for circa, about

indicators.note: wandering means the letters of four roam into a new order

explanation.surface: Roughly four people were discovered wandering on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Corfu is a Greek island in the Ionian Sea.

clue.text: Contribution sometimes burnt

definitions.meaning: a donation, as in a church collection

explanation.surface: A donation is occasionally set on fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift to a collection is a donation, and a burnt sacrifice was an offering to gods.

clue.text: Diana evidently has birthmarks

indicators.note: has means the words Diana evidently contain the answer within them

explanation.surface: A woman called Diana apparently has some birthmarks.
explanation.definitionFit: Naevi is the plural of naevus, a medical term for a mole or birthmark.

clue.text: South African robe gets torn

indicators.note: torn apart, the letters of robe are put together differently

explanation.surface: A South African's gown is ripped.
explanation.definitionFit: A Boer is a South African of Dutch descent, an Afrikaner.

clue.text: Inca's horse destroyed flowers

indicators.note: destroyed means the letters of Inca's horse are broken up and rebuilt

parts.note: the possessive s counts here as a letter

explanation.surface: An Inca's horse tramples a flower bed.
explanation.definitionFit: China roses are flowering shrubs, roses originally from East Asia.

clue.text: Shrewdly, like an expression of disapproval to-the City

parts.note: as means like
tut is a sound of disapproval
Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: Someone tuts disapprovingly at the City of London, cleverly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the City' looks like London's financial district; it is Ely, a small English cathedral city in Cambridgeshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Astute means sharp or canny, so the adverb means cleverly.

clue.text: Necessitate limitation

definitions.meaning: to require or involve as a consequence
a legal settlement restricting who may inherit property

explanation.surface: Someone states that a restriction is required.
explanation.definitionFit: To entail is to involve as a consequence, and an entail is a legal restriction on inheritance.
